newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. county to appeal $1 billion Lilco refund.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. county to appeal $1 billion Lilco refund.

text.p: New York's Suffolk County said Friday it will appeal a state court ruling that grants the Long Island Lighting Co. up to $1.16 billion in refunds and interest for overtaxing its Shoreham nuclear power plant.

If upheld, the decision issued Thursday could financially devastate Suffolk County, Brookhaven Town and the Shoreham-Wading school district, county officials said. Suffolk County is the eastern end of Long Island.
New York Gov. George Pataki and the Long Island Power Authority have said they would seek to cushion any adverse impact on residents, if the refund was implemented.
"There'll be protection for Suffolk County taxpayers," Rick Belyea, press secretary for Suffolk County's executive office, said. "There's no immediate tax increase on the horizon."

Lilco was recently awarded an $81 million refund for excess property taxes on its Shoreham nuclear power station while it was under construction. Lilco dropped out of the project in 1989 and decommissioning began in 1992.

Joseph McDonnell, vice-president of external affairs with Lilco, said in a statement that the payments "significantly increased the costs of the Shoreham project and the cost of electricity on Long Island."

Lilco customers pay some of the country's highest electricity rates, which were driven up by huge costs linked to closing and decommissioning Shoreham. The plant was closed due to environmental concerns before it began production.
